Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

watch nowNvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk." President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard."Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.Shares of Nvidia closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6."I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process."Stock Chart IconStock chart iconNvidia stock chart.Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That update prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people said. Huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations. Trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump said the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy." He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.""On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote. Several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected."Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.Read more Nvidia newsNvidia shares fall as Huang comeback rally coolsAG Blanche, FBI's Patel dodge questions about Huang investigationCongress blasts Nvidia bringing Jensen Huang backJensen Huang to face Congress the same day as Nvidia GTCWhat Jensen Huang's return means for Nvidia's Colette KressTrump: 'I made the deal' to reinstate Nvidia's HuangNvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade nowFor weeks following Huang's ouster, the company's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it.""The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company."Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China. Lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips."The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement Monday. Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his plans to testify.Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., said Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls.""Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday.WATCH: The rise, reinvention and uncertain future of Nvidia without Jensen Huangwatch now

Ladybird is now in alpha

Ladybird is now in alpha

Hello friends! Ladybird is now in alpha. You can download it for macOS and Linux. I’ve been looking forward to writing this post for a long time. :^) Ladybird is a browser with a new engine. The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork. The browser around it is modest, but functional. This is an alpha, so some websites won’t work, and it will crash sometimes. When that happens, tell us! You can report a broken site from inside the browser. After a crash, you can read the crash report and decide whether to send it. Our privacy policy has the details. We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today. When you pwn us, please tell us how so we can harden Ladybird! The alpha is a rolling channel, and we’ll be pushing out automatic updates regularly. This is the part I’m most excited about. Ladybird improves quickly, and until now you had to build it from source to see that. If you build websites, try yours in Ladybird and tell us what breaks. It supports WebDriver for automated testing, as well as the Firefox DevTools protocol. Thank you to our sponsors and donors, and to everyone who has tested, reported bugs, and written code over the years. There’s still a mountain of work ahead of us, but I’m very happy that you can finally try Ladybird for yourself!

Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis Joint statement by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative. On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code. We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement. Our rationale is outlined below. The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proof's correctness. We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct. The four criteria in https://xenaproject.wordpress.com/2026/11/12/and-the-proof-is-checked-in-lean/ are all satisfied.

We identified 177 GW of planned BYOP gas capacity—enough to power 65% of all US homes. Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to standardize parts to lower costs

Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to standardize parts to lower costs

Toyota, Nissan, and Honda will begin standardizing some vehicle parts in an effort to lower production costs, according to a report by Automotive News. The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses.Discussions are starting with Japan’s domestic suppliers, though international suppliers will be looped in soon.Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images|Getty ImagesThe first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”➡️ Skip the lot. His new goal is to delay the inevitable demise of his 2010 Volkswagen Golf.

Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as 'biggest breakthrough in decades'

Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as 'biggest breakthrough in decades'

A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades.In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body.Though doctors have said the pill cannot yet be considered a cure, and they do not know how long it can keep the disease at bay, they have said it is encouraging news because it appears it will offer patients more time, even if it does not cause full remission.Half of all people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer die within three months, and only about 3% of patients survive for five years when the disease spreads to other organs. It has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK and has a similarly poor prognosis globally.Patients were followed for a year and a half during the trial on average and some did not see the cancer return during this period. Longer studies will be conducted to see if any of the cancers can be put into remission. During the trial, tumours stopped growing in 90% of patients, just over 60% of patients had their tumours shrink or disappear, and for about 8% of patients tumours became undetectable on CT scans.A year after starting treatment, 76.6% of patients were alive; usually 40-45% of patients given chemotherapy alone survive a year.Dr Wungki Park, a gastrointestinal medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, who presented the findings, said “this is the closest to cure”, adding that he had never seen so many tumours disappear in patients whose cancer had spread.He presented the findings at the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona. “We are beginning to see not only a higher percentage of tumour response rates, but also deeper responses and a near doubling in the duration of disease control, which may eventually translate into longer survival,” he said.“The median follow-up is 18 months. Just imagine, in an average of 18 months your disease just disappears on the CT scan … that’s closest to complete remission … it’s incredible.”Daraxonrasib is a KRAS inhibitor treatment, which works by locking on to and shutting off certain mutations found in most pancreatic cancers. These mutations drive tumour growth.There are hopes the treatment could work for dozens of other cancers because they can have similar mutations.Michelle Mitchell, Cancer Research UK’s chief executive, said more research was needed, but added: “This is the biggest leap forward we’ve seen in decades for pancreatic cancer patients and could offer real hope to people facing one of the deadliest and most difficult-to-treat cancers.“These results raise the exciting possibility that this breakthrough could eventually pave the way for treating other cancers that carry Kras gene mutations. More trials are now needed before this treatment can be assessed for use on the NHS and despite this advance, pancreatic cancer survival is still very low.”

30 岁前的最后一年，究竟什么样才能做到 30 而立呢

30 岁前的最后一年，究竟什么样才能做到 30 而立呢

经朋友提醒，晚上看了一下日历才知道，今天居然是自己 29 岁生日。虽然我一直不是一个对生日很有执念的人，但是这次生日总有种排解不了的郁闷感。 24 的时候结了婚，25 岁有了孩子，前两年又经历出轨、离婚、自杀，但时间一分不少的叠加在了身上，还是不知不觉到了 30 岁前的最后一年。 刚刚看到论坛另一个帖子，也在聊人到 30 的一些感触，但下意识里，会觉得他像是上一辈的人一样，对这个话题充满敬畏，然后才意识到自己跟他不过是同龄人罢了。 前年五一前后，我因为严重的心理疾病，别人劝我去做些体力劳动，于是去了富士康找了份临时工作。很难说是运气好还是不好，以为自己要从事纯体力劳动，结果被分配去了机床维护，大部分时候比预想的要清闲很多，反而给了自己很多胡思乱想的机会，分心就会被模具烫伤，那时候车间里生产的还是 iPhone16，进场前还幻想着会不会遇到苹果的折叠机，结果折叠机 17 才出。 当时还在跟前妻拉扯离婚，虽然很清楚自己绝不可能原谅她，但又会下意识不相信跟她一开始的感情全是虚假。加上毕竟有一个还小的孩子，虽然不知道怎么样是对的，但总觉得可能更多责任应该归结于自己。 最不能释怀的是，我和前妻认识开始第二天同居，到结婚 4 年间里基本加起来不在一起的时间不超过 3 个月。而那个出轨者是在她怀孕期间，我怕她一个人代表焦虑，让她可以自己直播聊聊天打打游戏，以此认识的。 “跟他在一起的三个月，比跟你在一起的几年都快乐！” 吵架时后她吼出的这句话是我时至今日也会做梦惊醒的敏感点。我从来没想过这么经典的话会出现在自己身上，最走不出来的时候，我坐在开发区的烂尾楼顶，听着风吹过，看着长草的楼板上沙子刮起来打着旋…… 纵使种种，没想到还是到了这个年龄。以为自己永远会是那个打游戏看番的年轻人，不知道该怎么面对 30 而立这个说法。 今天早上虽然是自然醒，但不至于浪费掉一个上午，在家洗了洗最近积攒的衣服，还打扫了卫生；中午去吃了双 11 抽到的特价麦当劳套餐，薯条也是新鲜现炸的，最好吃的口感；下午打了游戏，稍微写了点项目，之前一直想看到没找到资源的银翼杀手 2049 也看到了（以前老是找到旧版）；晚上买到了这两天心心念念的凉菜和烧肉，刚回到家朋友问起我什么时候生日，没想到居然就是今天。 虽然从来没想过要好好庆祝这个尴尬的生日，但刚刚写这个帖子回顾今天一天的时候真得觉得意外得挺好，这一天算不上过得多快乐，但绝不算浪费生命的一天，甚至会想，如果不是最近遇到了想做的项目，而且很有起色，大概率今天会是早上睡觉，一觉睡到晚上 7 8 点，被人告知生日后随便吃点然后以庆祝为由喝不少酒吧…… 不好意思讲得很混乱，而且应该不太会有人全部看完吧。总之虽然完全不知道自己应该怎么走上 30 而立的人生，但祝自己生日快乐，今年的生日愿望是，自己和家人身体健康！如果有朋友看到这里，也祝你和家人身体健康！
